issues.claim: "review letters need point-by-point answers under N.J.A.C. 7:8" (section 3, "Now")
issues.problem: Regulatory misattribution. N.J.A.C. 7:8 is the stormwater management rule and sets design/performance standards (7:8-1.1 scope: stormwater management plans and stormwater control ordinances); it does not require point-by-point answers to municipal review letters. Point-by-point response letters are a board-engineer/application-completeness practice that covers all comments (zoning, utilities, sight distance, COAH), as the Riverdale minutes themselves show. The cited NJDEP page also could not be opened directly (Incapsula bot wall), so this assertion has no verified support at all. A P.E. reader would catch it.
issues.fix: Rewrite as two separate statements, e.g. "...and review letters need point-by-point answers, with stormwater comments judged against N.J.A.C. 7:8." Cite the NJDEP rule text (https://dep.nj.gov/wp-content/uploads/rules/rules/njac7_8.pdf) for the stormwater standards and avoid implying the rule governs the review-letter process.

issues.claim: "the firm's announcement says two long-serving staff have moved to part-time advisory roles ahead of retirement" (section 3 "Now" and the Sources list)
issues.problem: Partly unsupported. The announcement names Fred Coco and Jule Szalay taking part-time advisory roles as they begin the move to retirement, but says nothing about their length of service. "Long-serving" is the auditor's inference stated as fact; the firm's own page only says the officers have been "with our Firm for many years" and refers to "the past 50 years" generally.
issues.fix: Drop "long-serving" or replace with the sourced wording: "two principals have taken part-time advisory roles as they move toward retirement".

issues.claim: "...protect the track record from visitors and from the assistants people now ask for recommendations" (email draft)
issues.problem: Unlabelled inference. No cited source shows that buyers ask AI assistants for civil-engineering recommendations; it is a plausible market argument, not a fact, and it is the only unsupported claim in the founder-facing email, which otherwise tracks the site exactly.
issues.fix: Soften to opinion: "and from clients who now start with an AI search" or "we think assistants are increasingly where recommendations get asked for".

issues.problem: No arithmetic error found (recomputed: 17-64 h -> $1,069-$4,025; 82-220 h -> $5,157-$13,838; 24-153 h -> $1,509-$9,623 at $62.90/h), but each upper bound multiplies the maximum of every assumption at once, and section 3's top end (48 cycles x 8 h x 40%) is the least defensible for a firm of this size.
issues.fix: Optional: add one clause noting the top of each range assumes every assumption lands at its maximum, so the midpoint is the fairer planning figure.
